clue.text: Greek character's collared by drunk philosopher

indicators.note: to be collared is to be held round the neck, so the Greek letter sits inside the word for a drunk

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
phi is a Greek letter, with the possessive S kept

explanation.surface: A Greek is grabbed by a drunken thinker in a tavern scuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A sophist was a paid teacher of rhetoric and reasoning in ancient Greece, so a kind of thinker.

clue.text: One who soothes a charger

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who salves, applies a balm
second meaning: a charger is a large flat dish

explanation.walkthrough: 'Charger' looks like a warhorse but is a serving platter.
explanation.definitionFit: A salver is a tray for serving, and literally one who applies salve to ease pain.

clue.text: Do to keep one's equivalence

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the party holds the one

parts.note: a do is a party
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Throwing a party to maintain status with one's peers.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside PARTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Parity is the state of being equal, so it means equality or equivalence.

clue.text: Totally unconcerned at home, with a very small amount of money, not able to include one

parts.note: in means at home

parts.words: a very small amount of money
parts.note: a sou was a French coin of tiny value

indicators.note: to include is to take in, so the one goes inside

parts.note: can't means not able
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone at home and almost broke is perfectly relaxed about it.
explanation.walkthrough: A sou was an old French coin of tiny value, hence the phrase 'not a sou'.
explanation.definitionFit: Insouciant means carefree and nonchalant, showing no concern at all.

clue.text: Orchestral passage — dear me, it's over!

parts.note: tut is an exclamation of disapproval like dear me

indicators.note: over here means turned over, so the word reads backwards in this down clue

parts.note: it is taken as written, the 's being a link

explanation.surface: A disappointed listener sighs as the concert piece ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's over' sounds like the end of the music, but in a down clue 'over' turns the word upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti is a passage played by the whole orchestra together, from the Italian for all.

clue.text: One's involved in backing country's diet

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be wrapped up inside it, so these letters go within
backing means going in reverse, so the country is read from right to left

parts.note: Niger is a West African country
one, speaking of oneself, can be me

explanation.surface: A person's part in reversing the nation's food policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' standing for the speaker gives ME rather than the usual I.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed course of eating or exercise, much as a diet is.

clue.text: Espresso's lousy — take it back!

indicators.note: lousy means bad or poor, here a signal that the letters are in a mess

explanation.surface: A café customer sends back a bad coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of ESPRESSOS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To repossess is to reclaim goods not paid for, so the clue's imperative to reclaim fits.

clue.text: What greedy consumers do about Cork County

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a plug is a cork or stopper
Down is a county of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: What hungry diners do, set near Irish County Cork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cork County' looks like an Irish county; Cork is PLUG reversed and County is DOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: To gulp down food is to swallow it greedily in large mouthfuls.

clue.text: Artist from China, imbued with strength of character

indicators.note: something imbued with a quality has it inside, so the grit goes within

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), a friend
grit is courage and resolve

explanation.surface: A painter from China full of determination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but in Cockney rhyming slang china plate means mate, a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: René Magritte was a Belgian surrealist painter, an instance of the class of artists.

clue.text: Informant? I dispute that with raging fire!

parts.note: a protest of 'not I' disowns a claim

indicators.note: raging means wild or out of control, so the letters are tossed about

explanation.surface: An accused man denies starting a raging blaze.
explanation.walkthrough: NOT I, then FIRE rearranged as FIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A notifier is one who gives notice, so someone who passes on information.

clue.text: Day daughter omitted to follow Latin primate?

indicators.note: omitted means left out, so the daughter's letter is dropped from the singer's name

parts.note: Doris Day was an American film star and singer
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A Latin animal follows the actress once her daughter is left out.
explanation.walkthrough: Doris Day, the actress, loses D to give ORIS, which follows L.
explanation.definitionFit: The loris is a small nocturnal tree-dwelling monkey relative of South Asia; the question mark flags an example of the class.

clue.text: Excellent T-shirt on fellow at fair?

parts.note: a T-shirt is a type of top
F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS
fair hair or skin is light in colour

explanation.surface: Someone wearing a T-shirt at a funfair looks great.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' looks like a fairground but means pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-flight describes the highest class or quality, so first-rate.

clue.text: Relish being shut off in Amiens, surprisingly

indicators.note: the letters end up in a surprising arrangement, so the words are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; Amiens is a city in northern France

explanation.surface: Someone's delight at being locked out in a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of SHUT and AMIENS together are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Relish as a noun means keen enjoyment or zest, which is what enthusiasm is.

clue.text: Be annoying, when a good chap abandons dog

indicators.note: something that abandons a place leaves it, so these letters are taken out of the dog

parts.note: a mastiff is a large breed of dog
ST, saint, is a good person

explanation.surface: It is irritating when a decent fellow walks out on his dog.
explanation.walkthrough: A and ST leave MASTIFF, taking out the AST run.
explanation.definitionFit: To miff is to irritate or offend, so the verb fits an imperative sense of causing annoyance.

clue.text: Gather electronic device is a pest

parts.note: to harvest is to gather in a crop
a bug is a hidden listening device

explanation.surface: Collecting a surveillance gadget is a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pest' looks like a nuisance, but it is the literal mite.
explanation.definitionFit: A harvest bug is a mite larva whose bite irritates the skin, a garden pest in late summer.

clue.text: Gossip needs time to enter name and two temporary initials in account

indicators.note: to enter is to go into, so the letter for time goes inside the name

parts.note: a title is a name

indicators.note: in places the two letters inside the account

parts.note: a tale is an account or story
the initial letter of temporary, taken twice

explanation.surface: A rumour-monger's report needs dates and initials inserted.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes into TITLE, and TT (two initials of 'temporary') goes into TALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tittle-tattle is idle chatter about other people, a reduplicated word for gossip.

clue.text: Full of gas, it goes up in nasty vat leak

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the jumbled leak
nasty means unpleasant or messy, so the letters are rearranged
in a down clue going up means read from bottom to top, so the word is turned round

explanation.surface: Fumes rise from a horrible leaking vat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Full of gas' looks like the leak's fumes, but gas is idle chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of gas is slang for chattering endlessly, so a chatty person is talkative.

clue.text: One bent on disrupting airline's return route somehow?

indicators.note: a return trip goes back, so the airline letters are read in reverse

parts.note: BA is British Airways, with its S kept

indicators.note: somehow means in some unclear way, so the letters are arranged differently

explanation.surface: A troublemaker scrambles an airline's return flight path.
explanation.walkthrough: BA is British Airways, a crossword staple for 'airline'.
explanation.definitionFit: A saboteur deliberately wrecks or obstructs things, so is set on causing disruption.

clue.text: Top shelf made suitable for high living?

definitions.note: the definition describes a place, a noun, as somewhere for high living

indicators.note: to be made suitable the letters are adapted and reordered

explanation.surface: Putting luxuries on the top shelf befits a lavish lifestyle.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of TOP SHELF are rearranged; the answer is a place for indulgent living.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleshpot is a place offering luxury and sensual pleasure, a haunt of debauchery.

clue.text: Exhausted and is taken aback by '5' in part of crossword that's comprehensive

parts.note: all in is an informal phrase for exhausted

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the part of the crossword

parts.note: a clue is part of a crossword

indicators.note: taken aback is read literally as taken backwards, so the word is turned round

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A solver, worn out, is stumped by clue 5 in a puzzle covering everything.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted '5' looks like a cross-reference to 5 Across, but it is simply the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: All-inclusive means covering everything, as a holiday price might, so it is wide-ranging.

clue.text: Spur found to Cleopatra's right?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to goad or provoke
second meaning: Cleopatra's ... is an obelisk, the word following her name

explanation.walkthrough: In 'Cleopatra's Needle' the word sits to the right of her name; the obelisk stands on the Thames Embankment in London.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to prod or provoke them, just as a spur urges a horse.

clue.text: Most outstanding head moves down, as pests do

indicators.note: in a down clue moving down shifts a letter lower, so the top letter is relocated

parts.note: finest means best, most outstanding
the head of the word, its first letter F

explanation.surface: The top person is moved down, just as vermin swarm.
explanation.walkthrough: The F at the head of FINEST moves down one place.
explanation.definitionFit: Pests infest a place by overrunning it in large numbers.

clue.text: Sack author who's ditched two leading characters

indicators.note: ditching the two leading characters drops the opening pair of letters of the author's name

parts.note: Marcel Proust was a French novelist

explanation.surface: Firing a writer who has cut two main figures from his novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' looks like people in a novel, but here they are letters: PR goes from PROUST.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack someone is to dismiss them from a job, to remove or expel them.

clue.text: Fancy gemstone inlaid with an exotic fruit

indicators.note: something inlaid with a material has it set inside, so the article goes within
fancy as an adjective means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An ornate jewel set into a tropical fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The mangosteen is a tropical Asian tree whose purple-skinned fruit has sweet white segments.

clue.text: John gains name on the inside

indicators.note: on the inside means placed within, so the name letter goes inside

parts.note: gets means gains or obtains

explanation.surface: A man called John acquires a name for himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a man but is US slang for a toilet; N goes inside GETS.
explanation.definitionFit: John is American slang for a lavatory, and the Gents is a men's public toilet.

clue.text: See 6
Report: 'Former political organisation is on rocks'

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
the PLO is the Palestine Liberation Organization

indicators.note: rocks as a verb means shakes about, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A press statement about a former party that is now foundering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' looks like a news item but means a loud bang; 'on rocks' looks like a failing party but is an anagram of IS ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is the sharp noise of a gun or a blast, so a bang.

clue.text: Move made by bird that's lost its independence

indicators.note: something lost is no longer there, so the letter is taken away from the bird

parts.note: a budgie is a budgerigar, a small parrot
I is the abbreviation for independence or independent

explanation.surface: A pet bird that has lost its freedom tries to make a move.
explanation.walkthrough: BUDGIE without I.
explanation.definitionFit: To budge is to shift position slightly, so it means move, usually in the negative.

clue.text: Herb carries, ultimately, the can for VIP's team?

indicators.note: a thing that carries something holds it within, so these letters go inside the herb

parts.note: rue is a bitter aromatic herb

indicators.note: ultimately means at the last, so the final letter of the word is used

parts.note: last letter of the
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Someone named Herb takes the blame for a celebrity's staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb' looks like a man's name and 'carries the can' like taking the blame, but Herb is a plant and the can is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is the group of attendants who accompany an important person.

clue.text: Part of group, including FBI agents

indicators.note: including means holding within, so the agents go inside the group

parts.note: a set is a group
G-men is US slang for FBI agents

explanation.surface: A section of a gathering contains federal agents.
explanation.walkthrough: G-men, short for government men, is old American slang for FBI agents.
explanation.definitionFit: A segment is a portion or section of a whole, so one piece of it.
